name: tree-of-thoughts
context: Complex reasoning tasks where a single linear reasoning chain is insufficient and the agent must explore multiple alternative reasoning branches. The agent generates intermediate thoughts as nodes, evaluates their promise, and explores the most promising branches using breadth-first or depth-first search before committing to a final answer.
benefits: Systematic exploration of alternative reasoning paths
Backtracking from bad branches preserves correctness
Improves output quality on hard reasoning benchmarks
Explicit reasoning tree is highly observable
tradeoffs: Exponential branching increases cost and latency
Requires a good evaluation function to prune branches
More complex implementation than linear CoT
use_cases: Code debugging with alternative fix paths
avoid_when: Simple tasks where a single pass suffices
No reliable evaluation function for branches
anti_patterns: Exploring too wide without depth first
design_principles: Generate before evaluating — explore all branches fairly
Prune with value estimates, not just length
best_practices: Start breadth-first, switch to depth-first when a strong candidate emerges
Store failed branch summaries to avoid repeating dead ends
Use the LLM itself as the branch evaluator when no external signal exists
references: Yao et al., Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models, 2023 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10601
